   *(Introduction)*
   The `\rowcolor` command in LaTeX is used to apply a background color to an entire row in a table. It requires the `colortbl` package, but it's usually loaded via `xcolor` with the `table` option.

   *(Basic Usage)*
   Syntax: `\rowcolor{<color>}` placed at the beginning of a row (before the first cell content).
   Colors can be predefined (e.g., `red`, `blue`, `gray!20`) or custom-defined.

   *(Minimal Working Example)*
   ```latex
   \documentclass{article}
   \usepackage[table]{xcolor} % Loads colortbl automatically
   \begin{document}
   \begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
   \hline
   \rowcolor{blue!20} Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\ \hline
   Row 1 & Data & Data \\ \hline
   \rowcolor{yellow} Row 2 & Data & Data \\ \hline
   \end{tabular}
   \end{document}
   ```

   *(Important Notes/Pitfalls)*
   - Must load `xcolor` with `[table]` option (or load `colortbl` directly)
   - Place `\rowcolor` at the very start of the row, before any cell content or `\\`
   - Incompatible with some packages like `booktabs` (colors may bleed over rules). Workaround: use `\arrayrulecolor` or adjust spacing, or avoid `booktabs` with colored rows.
   - With `longtable`, `\rowcolor` works but may need careful placement.
   - If using `array` package, load `xcolor` after it to avoid conflicts.

   *(Related Commands)*
   - `\columncolor{<color>}` (in column definition: `>{\columncolor{...}}l`)
   - `\cellcolor{<color>}` (inside a single cell)
   - `\rowcolors{<start>}{<odd color>}{<even color>}` for alternating row colors

   *(Best Practices)*
   - Use light tints (e.g., `gray!15`, `blue!10`) for readability
   - Avoid coloring rows with heavy vertical/horizontal rules
   - Consider `\rowcolors` for large tables instead of manual `\rowcolor`

The `\rowcolor` command in LaTeX colors the background of an entire table row. It is provided by the `colortbl` package, but the modern and recommended way to use it is via `xcolor` with the `table` option.

### 🔹 Minimal Working Example
```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[table]{xcolor} % Automatically loads colortbl

\begin{document}
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
\hline
\rowcolor{blue!20} \textbf{Col 1} & \textbf{Col 2} & \textbf{Col 3} \\ \hline
Normal row & data & data \\ \hline
\rowcolor{yellow!40} Highlighted & data & data \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{document}
```

### 🔑 Key Rules
- **Placement**: `\rowcolor{<color>}` must appear at the **very beginning of the row**, before any cell content or alignment characters (`&`).
- **Colors**: Use predefined names (`red`, `gray`, `cyan`) or mix tints (`blue!20`, `black!10`). Define custom colors with `\definecolor{name}{model}{spec}`.
- **Package order**: Load `\usepackage[table]{xcolor}` **before** packages like `array`, `tabularx`, or `longtable` to avoid conflicts.

### ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `! Undefined control sequence. \rowcolor` | Missing `\usepackage[table]{xcolor}` |
| Color bleeds over `\hline` or `booktabs` rules | `colortbl` doesn't play well with `booktabs`. Either avoid `booktabs` with colored rows, or use `\arrayrulecolor{white}\hline` to mask bleeding. |
| `\rowcolor` after `\\` throws error | Move it to the start of the next row: `\\ \rowcolor{...} cell1 & ...` |
| Inconsistent coloring in `longtable` | Place `\rowcolor` inside the table body, not in the header/footer templates unless wrapped properly. |

### 🔁 Alternatives & Related Commands
- **Alternating rows**: `\rowcolors{2}{gray!10}{white}` (place before `\begin{tabular}`)
- **Single cell**: `\cellcolor{red!15}` inside a cell
- **Entire column**: `>{\columncolor{blue!10}}l` in the column specifier
- **Disable coloring temporarily**: `\rowcolor{white}` or `\hiderowcolors` / `\showrowcolors` (with `xcolor`)

### 💡 Best Practices
- Use **light tints** (`!10`–`!20`) to maintain text readability.
- Avoid combining heavy grid lines with row colors; consider a cleaner, rule-light design.
- For large tables, prefer `\rowcolors` over manual `\rowcolor` for maintainability.
